sequel.d: a part added to a book or play that continues and extends it

sequence.d: a following of one thing after another in time

sequencer.d: (chemistry) an apparatus that can determine the sequence of monomers in a polymer

sequoia.d: either of two huge coniferous California trees that reach a height of 300 feet; sometimes placed in the Taxodiaceae

sequin.d: adornment consisting of a small piece of shiny material used to decorate clothing

sequined.d: covered with beads or jewels or sequins

sequestration.d: seizing property that belongs to someone else and holding it until profits pay the demand for which it was seized

sequela.d: any abnormality following or resulting from a disease or injury or treatment

sequoyah.d: Cherokee who created a notation for writing the Cherokee language (1770-1843)

sequent.d: following or accompanying as a consequence
